text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike in 401s for several enterprise customers after scheduled SSO key rotation at 03:30 UTC — 03:42 UTC saw peak. Traces show auth failures, multiple support tickets.

lina: Julie from Acme reported their integration started failing around 03:40 UTC — API returns 401 with `invalid_token` for long-lived sessions. Julie says users had to log back in. She shared logs and a curl that now 401s.

julie: Repro steps from customer: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token-from-previous-session>\" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate` -> 401. Happening for ~30% of active sessions.

mike: I'm oncall. Looking at auth service dashboards now. Frontend rate of `401` for sso-auth validation endpoint jumped at 03:38. Routing looks healthy. No infra autoscaling faults.

ashwin: jumping in — checking auth logs and key-rotation job. Initial suspicion: key rotation path accidentally invalidating active session cache entries. Pulling logs.

ashwin: log snippet from auth cache at 03:37:
```
2026-09-18T03:37:41Z auth-cache INFO key_rotate: starting rotation id=rot-2026-09-18-1
2026-09-18T03:37:42Z auth-cache WARN invalidate-prefix: pattern=active_session_* matched=0
2026-09-18T03:37:43Z session-validator ERROR validate: token_id=abcd1234 status=missing-cache-entry fallback-db=false
2026-09-18T03:37:43Z oauth-proxy ERROR token-verify: token=abcd1234 reason=unauthorized code=401
```
ashwin: note `matched=0` here — but later we see mass `KEY_EXPIRES` flags set. Something in the rotation code path flipped the cache namespace.

evan: checking the key-rotation controller in k8s. Controller logs show a new flag `invalidate_all_sessions=true` present in today's release that was supposed to be gated. That looks like the regression. Rolling through commit history now.

casey: I'm going to run a quick query to see how many user tokens failed vs issued.

casey: Query results: ~4.2k distinct tokens rejected between 03:38 and 03:46 UTC from 12 enterprise customers. Top impacted: Acme, NovaSys, and Beacon.

mike: Immediate mitigation options? Revert the rotation or flip the feature flag to avoid invalidating the session cache. If we rollback, we must be careful not to break other systems relying on new keys.

ashwin: I recommend rolling the key back to previous revision and disabling `invalidate_all_sessions` flag. We can then push a guarded rotation after we fix the cache-path.

evan: I'm initiating rollback now. Command: `kubectl -n authrollouts apply -f rotation-config-prev.yaml` and `kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-gateway` to clear in-memory states.

ops-bot: incident-note: rollback started by evan at 03:52 UTC.

evan: rollback applied. Waiting for pods to become ready.

mike: @ashwin once rollback completes, can you validate that tokens issued before 03:30 work again?

ashwin: running a smoke test against Acme token sample: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer abcd1234' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health` -> STATUS 200 OK.

julie: Confirmed from Acme — users can access again, forcing a few service refreshes and most sessions recovered. Thanks. :white_check_mark:

lina: Opening a support status update to affected customers now. Draft message: "We've identified a regression in our scheduled SSO key rotation that temporarily invalidated active sessions. We rolled back the rotation and restored access. We'll follow up with a technical postmortem and timeline." Any objections?

mike: send it. Add ETA for postmortem. Also notify sales/CS for impacted accounts.

ashwin: root cause details so far: a recent change to the rotation controller introduced an opt-in feature flag `invalidate_all_sessions` that defaulted to true in config templating for this run. The controller's cache invalidation path used an incorrect Redis key prefix in the new code path which caused active-session keys to be dropped rather than just the ephemeral signing-keys. Regression originated from commit `b4f3c9d` (auth/rotation) pushed in today's deploy.

casey: reproducer: run `scripts/rotation_sim.sh --test` which triggered the same prefix flip locally and showed sessions being removed. We have a failing unit test coverage gap for the prefix logic.

ashwin: fix is to: 1) add explicit namespace to Redis invalidation (`auth:keys:*` vs `auth:active_session:*`), 2) ensure feature flag defaults to false, 3) add integration test that runs in CI using redis-mock. I'll open a PR.

evan: ops follow-ups: ensure rotation controller has a canary window and cross-check validation metrics pre-commit. Also add a circuit-breaker that aborts invalidation if observed active-session misses spike > 0.1%.

ops-bot: incident-note: rollback completed at 03:58 UTC, access restored by 04:02 UTC. Total MTTA ~8m, MTR ~30m.

lina: Taking ownership of customer notifications and incident timeline. Julie, I'll send the drafted message now and add a note that sessions will be invalidated only when explicitly requested.

julie: Received and forwarded to Acme engineering. They appreciate the quick rollback.

mike: Next steps for postmortem: 1) Ashwin to PR fix and tests (due EOD), 2) Casey to add monitoring alert for session invalidation anomalies, 3) Evan to add canary gating on rotation controller, 4) Lina to send customer follow-ups and CS handshake.

ashwin: PR: auth/rotation fix in progress — will request review from @evan and @casey.

casey: I'll add an alert `auth.session.invalidation.rate` > 0.1% for > 5m to paging oncall.

mike: Good work team. Document this in postmortems folder and assign Sev2. We'll include the reproducible steps and the exact commit that caused the regression.

lina: I'll close the thread once the customer comms are out and the postmortem link is available.

ops-bot: Incident closed in Slack: access restored and rollback validated.

---
Follow-up checklist (copied into thread for actions):
- lina: send formal customer postmortem and timeline.
- ashwin: open PR with fix + tests, tag `auth` and `eng-sre`.
- casey: create alert for session-invalidation spike and QA test.
- evan: add rotation canary and feature-flag safety check.
- mike: attach incident report to internal postmortem and update severity.
- ops-bot: keep archived logs for 90 days for audit.
